newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Hundreds attend protest in Indonesian capital.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds attend protest in Indonesian capital.

text.p: Hundreds of supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri staged a protest outside Indonesia's parliament house on Tuesday in a show of strength for the ousted minority party leader ahead of May's general elections.
Chanting slogans and waving banners reading "Mega or Nothing," about 1,500 to 2,000 people demonstrated outside the building in central Jakarta for most of the day, witnesses said.

Scores of riot police watched silently and made no move to intervene, even when some protesters tore down a section of the metal fencing around parliament house and blocked the main thoroughfare past the building, the witnesses said.

They said three truckloads of armed troops were seen in the area earlier in the day but were apparently kept in reserve. Army helicopters hovered overhead for most of the six-hour protest, the witnesses said.
The protesters dispersed after a senior Megawati aide read out a statement criticising the government for helping oust her from the leadership of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

"We require the government to return the political rights of members of the PDI and (return) the leadership of the party, which was forcibly and illegally taken away, to the lawful central board under the leadership of Megawati Sukarnoputri," the statement said.

"We remind the government to respect the rights of the people as holders of the country's sovereignty and to behave in accordance with the principles of the state of law and the principles of a democratic country," it said.

Megawati, daughter of the late founding president Sukarno, was ousted from the PDI leadership by a government-backed faction last June. Authorities have said that faction now constitutes the genuine wing of the party.

Megawati has been barred from running in the May 29 general elections when her name and those of her supporters were omitted from the list of election candidates supplied by the government-backed faction.
Indonesia allows only three parties to contest elections -- the PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party -- and all candidates must be approved by the government.

Jakarta was rocked by its worst riots in two decades when members of the government-backed faction stormed the PDI headquarters in the city in July and evicted Megawati supporters from the building with the help of police.
At least five people were killed and 149 injured in the violence, the national human rights commission has said. Several buildings were damaged and dozens of vehicles were set on fire.
